# Instructions

:::boxy
[nf-core rnaseq pipeline](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq/3.23.0/docs/usage/)
:::

**Topics covered**

-   RNA-seq data processing with the nf-core/rnaseq pipeline
-   Mapping of short reads (STAR) and quantification of gene expression (Salmon)
-   Quality control and exploratory data analysis
-   Differential expression analysis (DESeq2)
-   Functional enrichment analysis (ORA & GSEA)

**Data**

All datasets are bulk RNA-seq. The codes are in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/biosustain/dsp_transcriptomics_27200-Data-driven-bioengineering).

-   🦠 ***Staphylococcus aureus*** — biofilm vs planktonic lifestyle over time, strains USA-100 and USA-500, from [Tomlinson *et al.*, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1099/mgen.0.000598) (GEO: [GSE163153](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE163153), PRJNA685119).
    Reference genomes are strain-specific: **USA-100** → N315 ([GCF_000009645.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000009645.1/)); **USA-500** → USA300_FPR3757 ([GCF_000013465.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000013465.1/)), its closest finished relative, as in the paper.
-   🧑‍🔬 ***Homo sapiens*** — primary airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells treated with dexamethasone, paired donor design, from [Himes *et al.*, 2014](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0099625) (GEO: [GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778), PRJNA229998).
    Reference genome: GRCh37 ([GCF_000001405.13](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000001405.13/)), RefSeq annotation.
-   🧫 ***Escherichia coli*** K-12 MG1655 — saccharin treatment vs control ([PRJNA1158806](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJNA1158806)). A small subsampled version is used for the hands-on **nf-core/rnaseq pipeline run** below (so it finishes within class time), and the full dataset is analysed in the extra practice chapters at the end of the book.
    Reference genome: [GCF_000005845.2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000005845.2/) (NCBI RefSeq: NC_000913.3).

The *S. aureus* and human count matrices were produced with the same nf-core/rnaseq pipeline and are provided **precomputed** in the repository — the analysis notebooks start from those.

## Opening the Nextflow environment

To avoid installation and configuration issues we are going to deploy an environment for you containing Nextflow and its requirements.

If you want to open directly a GitHub codespace for this specific repository click here: [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/biosustain/dsp_transcriptomics_27200-Data-driven-bioengineering)

Before creating the Codespace, change the **Machine type** to **4-core** (click the options arrow next to the button instead of accepting the default). It says pay but you're not paying...

If you want to do it manually go to [course website](https://github.com/biosustain/dsp_transcriptomics_27200-Data-driven-bioengineering)

Click on button **Code** and click on the Codespaces tab. There click on **Create codespace**. Your environment is then started from the prebuilt image named in `devcontainer.json` — Ubuntu with Docker, Nextflow, R (and the Jupyter R kernel), Python and the AI agent CLIs already installed, running in VS Code in your browser.

To learn more about Github codespaces go [here](https://github.com/features/codespaces)


<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 Remember:</strong> Please remember to delete your Codespace by the end of the class so that you do not consume your free Github codespace credits! If you do not delete it it will be deleted automatically days after you created.
</div>


## Initial checks
Now, Nextflow should be ready to run in your GitHub Codespace environment! Let's check that you have a fully functional environment with Nextflow, java and Docker properly installed

**Verify java installation:**
```bash
java -version
```

**Verify Nextflow installation:**
```bash
nextflow -v
```

**Nextflow current version, system and runtime:**
```bash
nextflow info
```

**Verify Docker installation:**
```bash
docker --version
```

If everything went well you have a fully functional Nextflow environment for today. Remember that we are going to use VS code as our editor to write code and handle our files.


## AI assistants in your Codespace

AI-assisted workflows are allowed — and encouraged — in this course, as long as you **validate what the AI tells you**.

**In class, use GitHub Copilot Chat** — click the chat icon in the VS Code sidebar. It uses the GitHub account you are already signed in with (free for students via the [GitHub Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack)), so there is nothing to install or configure. It can read the files in this repository, explain code, and help you debug errors.

**Optional, for the curious:** your Codespace also has two *agentic* terminal assistants preinstalled — they can run commands and work through multi-step tasks, the kind of workflow discussed later in the course:

| Assistant | Where | Account needed |
|---|---|---|
| **Codex CLI** | Type `codex` in the terminal | OpenAI/ChatGPT login |
| **Claude Code** | Type `claude` in the terminal | Claude login (paid plan or institutional access) |

Fair warning: signing in from a Codespace takes a few extra steps — the browser pop-up flow does not work remotely, so choose the **device code** option and follow its instructions (for Codex you may first need to enable device authorization under ChatGPT **Settings → Security**). If that is more setup than you want, Copilot does everything you need for this session.

**Things to try**

- Ask: *"Explain what the design formula `~ donor + condition` does in the human differential expression notebook, and why donor is included."* Then check the explanation against the chapter text.
- Ask: *"Why does the quality control script round the Salmon counts before DESeq2 instead of truncating them?"* Verify the answer in the code.
- When a notebook cell errors, paste the error and ask the agent to diagnose it — then make sure you understand the fix before applying it.
- Ask an agent to interpret one of your PCA plots, and decide which parts of its answer the data actually supports.

<div class="warning">
  <strong>⚠️ Ground rules:</strong> AI assistants confidently make mistakes — treat every answer as a hypothesis to verify, not a fact. Never paste passwords, tokens, or API keys into a prompt. And you must be able to explain any AI-assisted result yourself.
</div>



## Data processing using the nf-core/rnaseq pipeline

**Sources of data and genome files**

For the hands-on pipeline run we use a **size-reduced *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 dataset** (reads: PRJNA1158806; genome: GCF_000005845.2) so the pipeline completes within class time. Nothing has to be downloaded — the subsampled reads and genome files are already deposited in the repository.

-   [RNAseq files (.fastq.gz) - PRJNA1158806](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJNA1158806)
-   [*E. coli* genome sequence (.fna.gz)](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/005/845/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz)
-   [*E. coli* genome annotation file (.gtf.gz)](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/005/845/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2/GCF_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.gtf.gz)

The ***S. aureus*** and **human** datasets analysed in the following chapters were processed with this same pipeline (aligner: `star_salmon`; for *S. aureus*, prokaryotic settings and strain-specific references). Their outputs — count matrices, gene lengths, and MultiQC reports — are provided precomputed under `data/`, so the analysis notebooks can start directly from the counts.
